{"id": 170, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — Veritas Row Revised SOW No. 2: Talvern custodian ESI processing and production (2025-07-09)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "VERITAS ROW DISCOVERY SERVICES LLC
REVISED STATEMENT OF WORK No. 2
July 9, 2025

Client: Harwick & Sloane LLP, on behalf of Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc.
Matter: Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877
Subject: Collection, processing, hosted review and production of Talvern custodian ESI

1. Supersession. This Revised Statement of Work No. 2 supersedes in its entirety the initial cost estimate issued by Veritas Row on June 25, 2025, which was prepared before custodian interviews were complete and is of no further effect. Pricing in this Revised SOW No. 2 is firm for the scope stated below.

2. Scope assumptions (as revised after custodian interviews conducted July 1-3, 2025):
   (a) Nine custodians (increased from the seven assumed in the initial estimate), including the operations, energy-desk and site-management custodians identified in the parties' ESI protocol.
   (b) Collected volume of 412 GB pre-processing (increased from 300 GB assumed).
   (c) Estimated review population after de-duplication, de-NISTing and date filtering: 61,000 documents.
   (d) Rolling productions in three waves, load files per the ESI protocol, with privilege log support.

3. Pricing.
   Line 1 — Forensic collection and chain-of-custody documentation, nine custodians: 58,300 dollars.
   Line 2 — Processing, promotion and hosted review platform, nine months of hosting: 121,400 dollars.
   Line 3 — Managed review, estimated 61,000 documents at the blended rate, including quality-control sampling and privilege screening: 196,800 dollars.
   Line 4 — Production, imaging, endorsement and load-file QC across three waves: 36,000 dollars.
   TOTAL PRODUCTION COST, Lines 1 through 4: 412,500 dollars.

4. Terms. Fees on Lines 1, 2 and 4 are fixed. Line 3 is capped at the stated figure absent a written change order signed by counsel. Invoicing monthly in arrears; payment net 30. This SOW incorporates the master services agreement between Veritas Row and Harwick & Sloane dated January 9, 2024.

Accepted and agreed:
Veritas Row Discovery Services LLC — D. Ellum, Director of Client Services
Harwick & Sloane LLP — A. Reyes, Partner"}

{"id": 171, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — Meet-and-confer letter: Harwick & Sloane to Dunmore Pell re revised production budget (2025-07-14)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "HARWICK & SLOANE LLP
Attorneys at Law — Minneapolis
July 14, 2025

BY EMAIL
Jonas Pell, Esq.
Dunmore Pell LLP
Counsel for Talvern Logistics Group LLC

Re: Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877 — meet and confer of July 11, 2025; Talvern custodian ESI production costs

Dear Mr. Pell:

This letter memorializes the parties' July 11 meet and confer under the Court's ESI protocol and Rule 26(f), concerning the cost of collecting, processing, reviewing and producing the Talvern custodian ESI hosted by our vendor, Veritas Row Discovery Services.

First, the parties agreed that the operative statement of the total production cost for the Talvern custodian ESI is the figure set out in Veritas Row's Revised Statement of Work No. 2 dated July 9, 2025: 412,500 dollars, covering nine custodians and three production waves. As we discussed, the vendor's earlier estimate of late June was prepared before custodian interviews, assumed a smaller custodian count and collection volume, and has been superseded; neither party will rely on it for any purpose, including cost-shifting argument.

Second, on allocation: without prejudice to either party's position on ultimate taxation of costs, the parties agreed to proceed on a 60/40 split of the total stated above (Meridian 60 percent, Talvern 40 percent), subject to reallocation by the Court on motion after substantial completion of the production waves.

Third, scheduling: wave one substantial completion by August 15, 2025; waves two and three at thirty-day intervals thereafter; privilege logs to follow each wave within twenty-one days.

If this letter does not accurately record your understanding of the July 11 conference, please advise in writing within seven days; otherwise we will treat the above as the parties' agreement and will so represent to the Court in the joint status report.

Very truly yours,
Adaeze Reyes
Partner, Harwick & Sloane LLP
Counsel for Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc."}
